review.note: Full citation: About Consolidated Logbook Data, whalinghistory.org. None, not peer-reviewed: the CoML part has a peer-reviewed methods paper (Smith, Reeves, Josephson and Lund 2012, PLoS ONE 7(4): e34905, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0034905), but most of the rows this layer uses are Maury's abstracts of the 1850s, which it does not cover.

aowl.coverage: About 1,500 logbooks of American and a few British offshore whaling voyages, 1784-1920; 468,249 rows. The layer uses the 446,337 rows of the two sources that log every day (Maury, CoML).
caveats: Encounters per logged day measure the hunt as well as the whale: ships went where they expected whales and chased them. It is not abundance.
Positions are off by about 2-3 degrees: noon was usually the only reading.
Many entries say only "Whale"; they are not counted, so rates are floors. Whaling History says in about 1 in 3 of Maury's abstracts "whale" should be read as right whale.
In and north of Bering Strait, logged "right whales" were more likely bowheads (Smith et al. 2012).
Maury's abstracts often leave out enclosed seas such as the Okhotsk and early North Atlantic legs.

After 1860 the logs are few and from one source (CoML): 37 voyages in the 1860s, 14 in the 1870s, 12 in the 1880s, 13 in the 1890s. A cell under 100 logged days or 3 voyages in a decade is no data, never zero. 76% of logged days fall in a cell shown.

Townsend (strike days only), IOSRW (right whale strikes added for one study), BSWF and Chatwin (mostly encounter days) are left out, since their days would count only encounters. On a day both Maury and CoML abstracted, CoML's row is used.
aowl.note: Readme of the 2025-09-16 release, saved at docs/design/licences/aowl-readme-20250916.txt. Preferred citation: American Offshore Whaling Logbook Data, https://whalinghistory.org, New Bedford Whaling Museum, Nantucket Historical Association, and Mystic Seaport Museum, Inc. The site's data pages also say "For research purposes, the complete database may be downloaded"; see licensing.md.

bbs.name: North American Breeding Bird Survey 1966-2023 (USGS and ECCC; Ziolkowski et al. 2024)
bbs.licence: No use restrictions (US Government data release, with Environment and Climate Change Canada); cite doi:10.5066/P136CRBV

review.evidence: USGS data release, Ziolkowski et al. 2024
review.quote: one data review and one metadata review, reconciliation, and Bureau approval.
review.note: Full citation: Ziolkowski, Lutmerding, English & Hudson 2024, U.S. Geological Survey data release (with Environment and Climate Change Canada). The DOI resolves to the ScienceBase item '2024 Release - North American Breeding Bird Survey Dataset (1966 - 2023)', which now says it 'has been superseded by a more recent release'. The quote is the USGS Fundamental Science Practices requirement for every USGS data release; the item page itself states no review. Counts are made by skilled volunteers under a fixed protocol.

bbs.coverage: About 5,300 roadside routes in the US and southern Canada (none in Mexico in this release), surveyed each June since 1966.
caveats: Counts from the roadside in June: a measure of where birds are detected, not of numbers or nests.
Smoothed between routes with a 75 km kernel over 5 years per slice: local detail is not real.
Only runs that met the survey's standards (RunType 1, primary observer).
bbs.note: Ziolkowski, D.J. Jr., Lutmerding, M., English, W.B. and Hudson, M-A.R. 2024, North American Breeding Bird Survey Dataset 1966-2023, U.S. Geological Survey data release.

eea-art17.name: Habitats Directive Article 17 species distributions, 2007-12, 2013-18, 2019-24 (EEA)
eea-art17.licence: CC BY 4.0 (EEA; stated on the 2007-12 and 2013-18 public datasets, and the EEA's default for its content)

review.quote: various stages of quality control have been built into the CDR data upload process
review.note: Full citation: European Environment Agency / European Topic Centre, Article 17 Habitats Directive reporting (Member State reports, EEA QA/QC). The quote is from the EEA's 'Delivery manual for Article 17 data' (14 March 2019, for the 2013-18 reports); it describes automated validation and QA/QC of format and consistency, not field checking. The distributions themselves are compiled by each Member State with its own methods; EU-level assessments are done by the EEA, ETCs and contractors (nature-art17.eionet.europa.eu). I did not find the equivalent manual for 2019-24.

eea-art17.coverage: EU member states (and the UK to 2018), 10 km grid, one map per six-year reporting period.
caveats: Reported by each member state with its own methods; public versions leave out sensitive records.
No data outside the EU: Switzerland, Norway, the Balkans and the east are blank, not empty of animals.
Spain and some others had no public 2019-24 distribution for some species at build time: no data there, not absence.
The 2019-24 service names no licence of its own; the EEA legal notice puts its content under CC BY 4.0 unless stated otherwise.
eea-art17.note: European Environment Agency, Conservation status of habitat types and species: datasets from Article 17, Habitats Directive 92/43/EEC reporting (public versions).

hornaday-1889.name: Map illustrating the extermination of the American bison (William T. Hornaday, 1889; Library of Congress g3301d.ct000308)
hornaday-1889.licence: US public domain: a US Government publication of 1889 (Government Printing Office). The Library of Congress is not aware of any US copyright protection.

review.evidence: Hornaday 1889, Report of the National Museum 1886-87
review.quote: the whole number of individuals of _Bison americanus_ now living is 1,091.
review.note: A museum curator's reconstruction from correspondents and his own expedition, published by the government in 1889, long before any review practice this scale means. Rights read from the Library of Congress item page at the Wayback Machine's capture of 23 Dec 2024, because loc.gov refuses automated readers; the scan is the copy on Wikimedia Commons, pinned by sha1.

hornaday-1889.coverage: North America, with ranges for 1870, 1875, 1880 and 1884, wild herds on 1 January 1889, and years the bison was gone by locality, from about 1720.
caveats: Hornaday's own reconstruction, from reports he gathered: neither a survey nor a modern estimate.

Lines are lifted from the map's inks through its printed graticule: control points typically about 11 km off when left out of the fit, and the map's towns about 25 km from where its graticule puts them.
The area once inhabited is undated, and mainly after J. A. Allen.
hornaday-1889.note: Hornaday, W. T. 1889, The Extermination of the American Bison, Report of the National Museum 1886-87, pp. 369-548. Method and proof: docs/design/hornaday-bison.md.

lcie-dryad.name: Large carnivore distribution maps for Europe, 2012-16 and 2017-22/23 (Kaczensky et al.; Ranc et al.; LCIE; Dryad)
lcie-dryad.licence: CC0 1.0 on both Dryad records (doi:10.5061/dryad.pc866t1p3, doi:10.5061/dryad.3xsj3txrc); no licence is stated in the files themselves

review.evidence: Kaczensky et al. 2024, report to the European Commission (IUCN/SSC LCIE)
review.quote: The mapping approach generally follows the methods described in (Chapron et al. 2014)
review.note: Compiled from national experts' maps by an IUCN specialist group. The README says the approach 'generally follows' Chapron et al. 2014 (Science) and Kaczensky et al. 2013, but that is not a methods paper for these maps, and no review of the maps themselves was found, so this is recorded as none.

lcie-dryad.coverage: Continental EU, Norway, Switzerland, the Balkans, Ukraine to a straight line in its west, European Turkey; 10 km grid; 2012-16 and 2017-22/23. Wolf, lynx, brown bear, wolverine in both, golden jackal in the later.
steps: presence.lcie (the zips can't be fetched by script: Dryad blocks it. Press Download dataset on doi:10.5061/dryad.pc866t1p3 and doi:10.5061/dryad.3xsj3txrc, unzip the first into .cache/lcie/v2021 and the second into .cache/lcie/v2024, leaving the inner zips zipped. Without them the build skips this set with a message and keeps its last entry; etl/presence/lcie.py has the file list.)
caveats: Hungary, Montenegro and Turkey were not fully mapped in 2012-16, so the later map can't be compared with it there: no data for 2012-16, even for the cells it has.
Golden jackal: the 2012-16 dataset used here has no jackal, so no data for that period, not absence. A separate map exists (Ranc et al. 2022, doi:10.5281/zenodo.6382215, CC BY 4.0, not used).
Ukraine is cut at a straight line and only European Turkey is included. The source gives no coordinates for the line, so coverage stops at the easternmost Ukrainian cell mapped.
PRESENCE has no status for much of the later map (58% of the jackal's cells, most of Italy's wolf cells, all of Finland's wolverine cells): status changes between the periods are not trends.
